body:
## Problem

`serviceTemplateString` substitutes only the placeholders `<NAME>`, `<DESCRIPTION>`,
`<USERNAME>`, `<COMMAND>`. Four lines instead reference the *shell* variable `$NAME`,
which the template never assigns (App.vue lines 44, 46, 49, 71). Every generated
script therefore expands `$NAME` to the empty string.

## Evidence

Generated with the default inputs, the emitted script contains (output line numbers):

```sh
30:     if pgrep -u $RUNAS -f $NAME > /dev/null
32:       echo "$NAME is now running, the PID is $PID"
35:       echo "Error! Could not start $NAME!"
57:     update-rc.d -f $NAME remove
```

`shellcheck -s sh` on the generated file confirms it:

```
line 30: ^---^ SC2154 (warning): NAME is referenced but not assigned.
```

With `$NAME` empty, line 30 degrades to `pgrep -u root -f` — a *valid* pgrep
invocation with no pattern, so it matches every process owned by RUNAS:

```
$ pgrep -u root -f ; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
stdout lines: 242
$ sh -c 'RUNAS=root; if pgrep -u $RUNAS -f $NAME >/dev/null; then echo "reports running"; else echo "reports error"; fi'
reports running
```

Line 57 degrades to `update-rc.d -f remove`, which consumes `remove` as the
service *name* and supplies no action.

## Impact

1. `start` unconditionally prints " is now running, the PID is <pid>" even when the
   service failed to launch. The failure branch on line 35 is unreachable, so a
   broken service reports success to the operator and to any wrapper script that
   scrapes the output.
2. `uninstall` deletes the init script (`rm -fv "$0"`) but the `update-rc.d`
   removal fails, leaving dangling `/etc/rc?.d/S??<name>` symlinks that point at a
   file that no longer exists.

## Fix

Add `<NAME>` to the variable block so the shell variable actually exists, and
substitute it like the others:

```sh
NAME=<NAME>
PIDFILE=/var/run/$NAME.pid
LOGFILE=/var/log/$NAME.log
```

Then quote both uses: `pgrep -u "$RUNAS" -f "$NAME"` and
`update-rc.d -f "$NAME" remove`. Also make the pgrep pattern match the actual
command rather than the service name, or drop the pgrep check entirely and test
the recorded PID with `kill -0`.

## Resolution
Added NAME=<NAME_Q> to the variable block and quoted both uses; start() now verifies the recorded PID with kill -0 instead of a patternless pgrep, and update-rc.d -f "$NAME" remove receives the name. Guarded by service-template.spec.ts.
title: $NAME is never assigned in the generated init script: start() always reports success, uninstall() never deregisters

body:
## Problem

All four inputs are substituted into the shell template with a bare
`String.replace(/<PLACEHOLDER>/g, value)` (App.vue:124-128 and 135-139). There is
no shell quoting, no escaping, and no character validation anywhere in the app.
The template's placeholders sit in unquoted assignment position
(`PIDFILE=/var/run/<NAME>.pid`) and inside double quotes (`SCRIPT="<COMMAND>"`),
so any shell metacharacter, quote, space, or newline in the input changes the
meaning of the generated program.

## Evidence

Service name `x; touch /tmp/PWNED #` produces:

```sh
PIDFILE=/var/run/x; touch /tmp/PWNED #.pid
LOGFILE=/var/log/x; touch /tmp/PWNED #.log
```

The generated init script runs `touch /tmp/PWNED` as root on every invocation.

Ordinary, non-malicious input breaks it just as reliably. Service name `my app`:

```sh
PIDFILE=/var/run/my app.pid
$ sh -c 'PIDFILE=/var/run/my app.pid'
sh: 1: app.pid: not found
```

Command `/usr/bin/node /srv/app.js --opt="x y"`:

```sh
SCRIPT="/usr/bin/node /srv/app.js --opt="x y""
```

Description `Line one\n# hijacked` escapes the LSB header block:

```sh
# Description:       Line one
# hijacked
### END INIT INFO
```

## Impact

The app's sole output is a file the user is instructed to place in `/etc/init.d/`
and run as root. A service name containing a space — entirely reasonable, and not
rejected by the UI — yields a script that fails at startup with a confusing
`app.pid: not found`. A name containing `;`, backtick, or `$(...)` yields root
command execution. Because the app has no URL-parameter or storage surface an
attacker cannot seed the fields remotely, so this is primarily a
foot-gun-and-breakage defect rather than a remote exploit — but the artifact it
produces is unsafe by construction.

## Fix

Two changes, both needed:

1. Restrict the service name and username at the input boundary to what the
   surrounding contexts can safely carry, e.g. `pattern="[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+"` plus a
   `<form>` so the constraint is actually enforced (see the separate finding on
   inert `minlength`), and reject anything else with a visible message.
2. Shell-quote every interpolation rather than trusting validation alone. Add one
   helper and use it for all four substitutions:

```ts
// single-quote for POSIX sh: wrap in '...', escaping embedded quotes as '\''
const shq = (s: string) => `'` + s.replace(/'/g, `'\''`) + `'`
```

Emit `SCRIPT=<shq(command)>`, `RUNAS=<shq(username)>`, `NAME=<shq(service)>`, and
strip newlines from the description before it enters the `#` comment block
(`description.replace(/[\r\n]+/g, ' ')`).

## Resolution
All interpolations now go through shq() (POSIX single-quoting) via fill(); service name and username additionally restricted to SAFE_NAME=/^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/ and enforced by a <form> with pattern=. Description passed through oneLine(). Injection and quoting cases covered by tests.
title: User input is interpolated unescaped into a script intended to run as root

body:
## Problem

The generated start command is built as:

```sh
local CMD="$SCRIPT &> \"$LOGFILE\" & echo \$!"
su -c "$CMD" $RUNAS > "$PIDFILE"
```

`&>` is a bash/zsh redirection operator. It is not POSIX. The script's own shebang
is `#!/usr/bin/env sh`, and the commented-out alternative on line 40 explicitly
forces `su -s /bin/sh`. `su -c` runs the string in the *target user's* login
shell, so the behaviour depends on that user's shell — on Debian/Ubuntu
`/bin/sh` is dash.

## Evidence

Under dash, `cmd &> file` parses as two commands: `cmd &` followed by
`> file &`. The redirect never attaches to the command, and `$!` returns the PID
of the *second* background job — the bare redirect — not of the service.

```
$ readlink -f /bin/sh
/usr/bin/dash

$ sh -c 'echo hello &> /tmp/ampgt.txt; echo "file contents: [$(cat /tmp/ampgt.txt)]"'
hello
file contents: []
```

Log output goes to the terminal; the log file is created empty. And the recorded
PID is wrong:

```
$ sh -c 'SCRIPT="sleep 40"; LOGFILE=/tmp/lg.txt; CMD="$SCRIPT &> \"$LOGFILE\" & echo \$!"; sh -c "$CMD" > /tmp/pidf'
PIDFILE contains: 3590285
actual sleep 40 pid(s): 3590282 3590284

$ sh -c 'P=$(cat /tmp/pidf); kill -0 "$P" || echo "pid $P DEAD"'
sh: 1: kill: No such process
pid 3590285 DEAD
```

## Impact

Every downstream operation that reads PIDFILE is broken whenever RUNAS's shell is
dash/sh:

- `stop` takes the `! kill -0` branch, prints "Service not running", returns 1,
  and never kills the real process — which keeps running, orphaned.
- `status` prints "The process appears to be dead but pidfile still exists".
- `restart` therefore never stops the old process, and `start` then either
  spawns a duplicate or refuses.
- Service stdout/stderr is discarded, so there is nothing to diagnose with.

The stale PIDFILE is also never cleaned up, so the leak persists across boots.

## Fix

Use POSIX redirection and capture the PID of the right job. Replace the CMD
construction with:

```sh
CMD="$SCRIPT >> \"$LOGFILE\" 2>&1 & echo \$!"
su -s /bin/sh -c "$CMD" "$RUNAS" > "$PIDFILE"
```

`>> file 2>&1` is POSIX and attaches to `$SCRIPT`, so `$!` is the service's PID.
Pin the shell with `-s /bin/sh` so behaviour no longer depends on the target
user's login shell — this makes the currently commented-out line 40 the only
form, and line 39-40's "try this instead if the above does not work" comment can
be deleted along with the broken variant.

## Resolution
Replaced &> with POSIX '>> "$LOGFILE" 2>&1' so the redirect attaches to $SCRIPT and $! is the service PID; su now pins -s /bin/sh. dash -n and shellcheck run in npm test.
title: `&>` is a bashism: under a /bin/sh shell the wrong PID is recorded and the log file stays empty, breaking stop/status/restart

body:
## Problem

Beyond the `&>` bashism filed separately, the template declares `sh` but uses
constructs that POSIX does not define, and leaves command substitutions unquoted
so any whitespace in a PID file splits into multiple arguments.

## Evidence

`shellcheck -s sh` on the generated script (default inputs) reports 7 warnings and
15 notes:

```
line 23: SC3043 (warning): In POSIX sh, 'local' is undefined.       # local CMD
line 51: SC3043 (warning): In POSIX sh, 'local' is undefined.       # local SURE
line 50: SC3037 (warning): In POSIX sh, echo flags are undefined.   # echo -n
line 18: SC2046 (warning): Quote this to prevent word splitting.    # kill -0 $(cat $PIDFILE)
line 40: SC2046 (warning): Quote this to prevent word splitting.
line 45: SC2046 (warning): Quote this to prevent word splitting.    # kill -15 $(cat "$PIDFILE")
line 52: SC2162 (info): read without -r will mangle backslashes.    # read SURE
line 18: SC2248 ... unquoted $PIDFILE / $RUNAS throughout
```

(`local` happens to work in dash, but not in every `sh`; `echo -n` prints a
literal `-n` in dash-derived shells.)

## Impact

`echo -n` emits a literal `-n ` before the uninstall confirmation prompt on any
shell whose `echo` lacks the flag, so the operator sees
`-n Are you really sure...`. Unquoted `$(cat …)` means a PIDFILE containing
whitespace or a glob character passes multiple arguments to `kill`, which then
either errors or signals an unintended PID.

## Fix

Quote every expansion and replace the non-POSIX constructs:

```sh
printf '%s' "Are you really sure you want to uninstall this service? [yes|No] "
read -r SURE
...
kill -0 "$(cat "$PIDFILE")" 2>/dev/null
kill -15 "$(cat "$PIDFILE")" && rm -f "$PIDFILE"
```

Drop both `local` declarations (the functions are not recursive, so plain
assignment is fine), and add `shellcheck -s sh` over the generated output to the
test suite so regressions are caught mechanically.

## Resolution
Dropped both 'local' declarations and echo -n (now printf '%s'), added read -r, quoted every expansion and command substitution. shellcheck -s sh is now clean at all levels (was 7 warnings + 15 notes).
title: Generated script uses six non-POSIX constructs under a `#!/usr/bin/env sh` shebang

body:
## Problem

`status()` decides whether the service is alive with:

```sh
if [ -z "$(ps axf | grep ${PID} | grep -v grep)" ]; then
```

This greps the entire `ps axf` output — every column, for every process on the
system — for the PID as an unanchored substring, instead of asking the kernel
whether that specific PID exists.

## Evidence

`ps axf` output contains PIDs, TTY names, accumulated CPU times, and full command
lines. A recorded PID of `123` matches the line for PID `1234`, a process whose
command line contains `123` (e.g. `node server.js --port 1230`), and a TIME field
of `1:23`. Conversely `grep -v grep` also discards a legitimate match when the
service's own command line contains the string `grep`.

## Impact

`status` reports "Running, the PID is 123" for a service that is dead, as soon as
any unrelated process on the box happens to contain those digits — which on a
busy host is close to always. That makes `status` useless as a health check and
unusable in monitoring.

## Fix

Ask about the PID directly:

```sh
if kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Running, the PID is $PID"
else
    printf '%s\n' "The process appears to be dead but pidfile still exists"
fi
```

`kill -0` is POSIX, needs no subshell, and cannot false-positive.

## Resolution
status() now uses kill -0 "$PID" instead of grepping ps axf output for the PID as a substring.
title: status() matches any process whose ps line merely contains the PID as a substring

body:
## Problem

`LOGFILE=/var/log/<NAME>.log` is written from inside the string passed to
`su -c "$CMD" $RUNAS`, i.e. the redirection is performed *after* privileges drop
to RUNAS. `/var/log` is `root:root` and mode `0755` on Debian/Ubuntu, so a
non-root RUNAS cannot create the file. Nothing in the script checks whether the
redirect succeeded.

## Evidence

Compare the two redirections in `start()`:

```sh
su -c "$CMD" $RUNAS > "$PIDFILE"   # runs as root  -> succeeds
      ^^^^ CMD contains: $SCRIPT &> "$LOGFILE"     # runs as RUNAS -> EACCES
```

The app's own UI advertises `root` only as the *default* username, and the field
exists precisely so a service can run as an unprivileged account. For any
RUNAS other than root, the inner redirect fails with
`/var/log/<name>.log: Permission denied` and the shell aborts that command —
so `echo $!` never runs and PIDFILE is left empty.

## Impact

For the documented non-root use case the service does not start at all, and the
only diagnostic — the log file — is the thing that failed. Combined with the
`$NAME` finding, `start` still prints "is now running", so the operator is told
the service came up when nothing was launched.

## Fix

Create the log file as root and hand it to RUNAS before dropping privileges:

```sh
start() {
  ...
  touch "$LOGFILE" && chown "$RUNAS" "$LOGFILE" || {
    echo "Error: cannot prepare $LOGFILE" >&2
    return 1
  }
  CMD="$SCRIPT >> \"$LOGFILE\" 2>&1 & echo \$!"
  su -s /bin/sh -c "$CMD" "$RUNAS" > "$PIDFILE"
```

Alternatively emit `LOGFILE=/var/log/<NAME>/<NAME>.log` with a root-created,
RUNAS-owned directory, which is what the accompanying logrotate config already
assumes it can rotate.

## Resolution
start() creates the log as root and chowns it to RUNAS before dropping privileges, and fails loudly with a message if that cannot be done.
title: Log file in root-owned /var/log is opened as the unprivileged RUNAS user, so output is silently discarded

body:
## Problem

The `### BEGIN INIT INFO` block provides `Provides`, `Required-Start`,
`Required-Stop`, `Default-Start`, `Default-Stop`, and `Description`, but not
`Short-Description`, which the LSB spec lists alongside `Description`. Separately,
`PIDFILE=/var/run/<NAME>.pid` targets `/var/run`, which has been a compatibility
symlink to `/run` since Debian 7 / systemd adoption.

## Evidence

`insserv` and `update-rc.d` emit
`warning: script '<name>' missing LSB tags and overrides` variants when the
header is incomplete; Debian Policy 9.3.1 documents the header fields.
`/var/run` is documented as deprecated in the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard 3.0
§3.15 in favour of `/run`.

## Impact

Cosmetic warnings during `update-rc.d` registration, and a PID path that relies
on a compatibility symlink no longer guaranteed to exist on minimal images.

## Fix

Add the field and switch the path in `serviceTemplateString`:

```sh
# Short-Description:  <DESCRIPTION>
# Description:        <DESCRIPTION>
...
PIDFILE=/run/$NAME.pid
```

## Resolution
Added '# Short-Description:' to the LSB header and moved the pidfile to /run/$NAME.pid. Asserted in tests.
title: LSB header omits Short-Description and PIDFILE uses the deprecated /var/run

body:
## Problem

`serviceTemplate` and `logRotate` are plain `let` bindings (lines 124-130). The
template renders them via `v-text`, but a plain `let` is not a reactive
dependency, so Vue never tracks them. A `watch` on the four inputs (lines
132-145) reassigns them, and separately reassigns `servicePath`, `logRotatePath`,
and `shellCommands`. The substitution logic is written twice — once for the
initial value, once inside the watcher — with no shared helper.

## Evidence

The UI is correct today only by coincidence of two Vue implementation details:
`watch` defaults to `flush: 'pre'`, which runs the callback *before* the
component re-renders, and the template independently reads reactive values
(`v-model="service"` and friends, plus `{{ servicePath }}`) which is what
schedules that re-render at all. Nothing in the code expresses either dependency.

The duplication is load-bearing: lines 124-128 and lines 135-139 must stay
byte-identical in their substitution order or the first paint disagrees with every
subsequent one.

Latent break — remove or relocate the reactive reads and the textareas freeze.
Moving the four inputs into a child component, or switching the paths to plain
strings, leaves nothing reactive in `<main>`, no re-render is scheduled, and the
generated script silently stops updating as the user types. No test or type error
would catch it.

## Impact

A future refactor that touches the template silently breaks the app's only
feature, with no failing test to signal it. The duplicated substitution block is
a standing correctness hazard, and the watcher is 14 lines expressing what the
framework does declaratively.

## Fix

Delete the watcher, both `let`s, and the three `ref`s, and derive everything:

```ts
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const fill = (tpl: string) =>
  tpl
    .replace(/<NAME>/g, service.value)
    .replace(/<DESCRIPTION>/g, description.value)
    .replace(/<USERNAME>/g, username.value)
    .replace(/<COMMAND>/g, command.value)

const servicePath = computed(() => '/etc/init.d/' + service.value)
const logRotatePath = computed(() => '/etc/logrotate.d/' + service.value)
const serviceTemplate = computed(() => fill(serviceTemplateString))
const logRotate = computed(() => fill(logRotateString))
const shellCommands = computed(
  () => `sudo chmod +x ${servicePath.value} && sudo update-rc.d ${service.value} defaults`
)
```

That is ~20 lines deleted, one substitution path instead of two, and the
dependencies become real rather than incidental. It is also where the shell
quoting from the injection finding belongs, since `fill` becomes the single
substitution point.

## Resolution
Deleted the 14-line watcher and both non-reactive lets; servicePath, logRotatePath, serviceTemplate, logRotate and shellCommands are now computed(). Substitution exists once, in fill(), extracted to src/service-template.ts.
title: serviceTemplate and logRotate are non-reactive `let`s kept fresh by a 14-line watcher; `computed` removes the whole mechanism

body:
## Problem

`App.vue` declares its four inputs with `defineModel()`:

```ts
const service = defineModel('service', { default: 'my-service' })
```

`defineModel` is the macro for a two-way *prop* binding: it compiles to a `prop`
plus an `update:<name>` emit, for use with `v-model` on a parent. `App` is
mounted directly by `createApp(App).mount('#app')` (src/main.ts:6) and has no
parent, so no prop is ever passed and no emit is ever consumed.

## Evidence

`src/main.ts` mounts `App` as the root with no props:

```ts
createApp(App).mount('#app')
```

`defineModel` therefore falls through to its `default:` every time, behaving as
local state — while still generating the props declaration and the four
`update:service` / `update:description` / `update:username` / `update:command`
emits. The generated `src/App.vue.js` shows the dead machinery
(`__VLS_defaultModels`, `__VLS_modelEmit`), all of it unreferenced.

## Impact

The component's public interface advertises four two-way bindings it does not
support, which is actively misleading to anyone reusing `App.vue` as a child —
they would pass `v-model:service` and see it work, then find local edits also
mutating their state. It is also the reason the type-check emit contains unused
model plumbing.

## Fix

Use the primitive that matches the intent — these are local state, not props:

```ts
const service = ref('my-service')
const description = ref('This command does something')
const username = ref('root')
const command = ref('/usr/local/bin/command')
```

`ref` is already imported. Nothing else in the file changes: `v-model` on an
`<input>` works identically against a `ref`.

## Resolution
Replaced the four defineModel() calls with ref(), removing the props/emits contract the root component could not honour.
title: defineModel() used for local state in the root component, declaring a props/emits contract that cannot exist

body:
## Problem

The four `<input>` elements carry `minlength="1"` but live in a `<header>` with
no `<form>` ancestor and no submit step. HTML constraint validation only runs on
form submission or an explicit `checkValidity()` call, so `minlength` never
blocks anything here. Nothing else in the component validates the inputs.

## Evidence

Clearing the "Service name" field yields, immediately and with no warning:

```sh
PIDFILE=/var/run/.pid
LOGFILE=/var/log/.log
# Provides:
```

and the UI's own instructions become `Save as: /etc/init.d/` and
`sudo chmod +x /etc/init.d/ && sudo update-rc.d  defaults`. `minlength` shows no
`:invalid` styling either, because the component defines none.

## Impact

The app silently emits a structurally invalid init script and instructs the user
to save it over the `/etc/init.d/` directory itself. This is also the enforcement
point the shell-injection finding depends on — without a real validation gate,
quoting is the only defence left.

## Fix

Wrap the fields in a `<form>` so constraint validation is live, and state the
character set the shell contexts can carry:

```html
<form @submit.prevent>
  <label>
    Service name:
    <input type="text" required pattern="[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+" v-model="service" />
  </label>
  ...
</form>
```

Add a `:invalid` style so the constraint is visible, and gate the output on
validity rather than rendering a broken script.

## Resolution
Wrapped the fields in <form @submit.prevent>, replaced inert minlength with required + pattern on the two shell-bearing fields, added per-field error messages and :invalid styling, and gated the output behind a validity check.
title: minlength="1" is inert with no <form>, so empty inputs generate a script with no service name

body:
## Problem

The three outputs render as `<textarea v-text="...">`. `v-text` sets
`textContent`, which for a `textarea` seeds the *default* value only. The control
stays editable, so users can type into it, but any re-render replaces their edits.
The README's usage step 2 is "Copy the generated template", yet there is no copy
button.

## Evidence

`v-text` compiles to a `textContent` binding, not a `value` binding — Vue's docs
direct `v-model` for form controls. Editing the "Generated service script"
textarea and then changing any input field discards the edit, because the
re-render rewrites `textContent`. Two of the three textareas are additionally
`class="noresize"` (`resize: none`, main.css:89-91), so a long generated script
cannot be expanded to read.

## Impact

Users lose hand-tweaks without warning, and the primary interaction the README
prescribes — copy the output — requires a manual select-all in a fixed-height,
non-resizable box.

## Fix

Mark the outputs as outputs and add the copy affordance:

```html
<textarea readonly :value="serviceTemplate" style="height: 400px"></textarea>
<button type="button" @click="navigator.clipboard.writeText(serviceTemplate)">Copy</button>
```

`readonly` makes the discard-on-rerender behaviour impossible rather than
surprising, and `:value` is the correct binding for a form control.
`navigator.clipboard` needs no dependency.

## Resolution
Outputs are now readonly with :value bindings instead of v-text, and each has a Copy button using navigator.clipboard.
title: v-text on <textarea> discards user edits and gives no copy affordance, though copying is step 2 of the documented workflow

body:
## Problem

`a` and `.green` are both coloured `hsla(160, 100%, 37%, 1)` = `rgb(0, 189, 126)`
(main.css:10-16). In light mode the page background is `--vt-c-white` = `#ffffff`
(base.css:3, 24). That pairing is used for the `<h1>` page title
(`class="green"`, App.vue:150) and the footer author link (App.vue:193).

## Evidence

Computed contrast ratios against the actual palette:

```
green rgb(0,189,126)
LIGHT MODE  green on #ffffff : 2.45:1  | AA normal (4.5:1) FAIL | AA large (3:1) FAIL
DARK  MODE  green on #181818 : 7.25:1  | AA normal (4.5:1) PASS
```

The failure is light-mode-only; the dark scheme is fine. For reference the rest of
the palette passes: body text `#2c3e50` on white is 10.98:1, dark-mode body text
composites to 6.71:1, and the textareas are 14.98:1.

The footer link is default body size (15px, base.css:80), so the 4.5:1 threshold
applies. The `<h1>` is 2.6rem/500 weight, which qualifies as large text at the
3:1 threshold — and 2.45:1 fails that too.

## Impact

WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (Contrast, Minimum, level AA) failure for the page's title and
its only link, for every visitor whose OS is set to light mode — i.e. the default
on most systems. Low-vision users cannot reliably read either.

## Fix

Darken the accent to reach 4.5:1 on white while keeping the hue, and let dark
mode keep the brighter value it already passes with:

```css
:root {
  --color-accent: hsl(160, 100%, 26%);   /* 4.63:1 on #ffffff */
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --color-accent: hsl(160, 100%, 37%); /* 7.25:1 on #181818 */
  }
}
a,
.green {
  color: var(--color-accent);
}
```

Then reuse `var(--color-accent)` for the textarea border (main.css:77) and the
hover background (main.css:48) so the accent is defined once.

## Resolution
Introduced --color-accent: light mode hsl(160,100%,26%) = 4.67:1 on white (was 2.45:1), dark mode keeps hsl(160,100%,37%) = 7.25:1. Added --color-error at 7.02:1 light / 6.60:1 dark. Accent now defined once and reused by link, heading, button and textarea border.
title: Link and heading colour fails WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in light mode at 2.45:1

body:
## Problem None of the three ` ... Logrotate ... Shell commands to run ``` A screen reader announces each of these as an unnamed "edit text" / "multi-line text field", with no indication of which of the three it is or what it contains. The "Save as:" path — the information the user needs in order to act on the content — is in a sibling `
` with no association either. ## Impact WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) and SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) failures. A non-sighted user reaching the outputs by keyboard cannot tell the init script apart from the logrotate config or the shell commands. ## Fix Give each output a name and tie the destination path to it: ```html

Generated service script:

Save as: {{ servicePath }}
``` Repeat for the two `
` outputs using their `` text as the label source. This composes with the `readonly` change in the `v-text` finding. ## Resolution Each output textarea now carries aria-labelledby pointing at its heading/summary, plus aria-describedby for the 'Save as' path. Asserted in App.spec.ts.
title: The three output textareas have no accessible name

body:
## Problem

The trailing `languageOptions` block sets `parserOptions.project`. Since
`@vue/eslint-config-typescript` v14, `vueTsConfigs.recommendedTypeChecked`
enables `projectService`, and typescript-eslint treats the combination as a fatal
configuration error. The block also sets `sourceType: 'script'` in a package
declaring `"type": "module"`, where every file is ESM.

## Evidence

```
$ npm run lint ; echo "exit=$?"
env.d.ts
  0:0  error  Parsing error: Enabling "project" does nothing when "projectService"
              is enabled. You can remove the "project" setting
src/App.vue
  0:0  error  Parsing error: Enabling "project" does nothing when "projectService" ...
src/main.ts
  0:0  error  Parsing error: Enabling "project" does nothing when "projectService" ...
vite.config.ts
  0:0  error  Parsing error: Enabling "project" does nothing when "projectService" ...
✖ 14 problems (14 errors, 0 warnings)
exit=1
```

Every one of the project's four real source files is a fatal parse error, so no
rule in the config is ever evaluated against any of them. The remaining errors
are against `src/App.vue.js`, `src/main.js`, and `vite.config.js` — generated
files that should not exist (filed separately).

No workflow runs this command. `pr-build.yml` runs only `npm run build`;
`pr-lint.yml` delegates to `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` (MegaLinter), which runs
its own linter set, not the repository's `eslint.config.mjs`. Meanwhile
`AGENTS.md:9` instructs "Run linting and type checks before committing any code
changes" — an instruction that cannot be satisfied.

## Impact

The repository has no working ESLint coverage at all. `eslint-plugin-vue`'s
`flat/essential` rules and the entire type-checked rule set are configured and
inert. Several defects in this audit — unused-variable and unquoted-expansion
classes of problem — are exactly what those rules exist to catch.

## Fix

Delete the trailing `languageOptions` block; `projectService` already resolves the
right tsconfig per file, and the empty `{ // your overrides }` placeholder above
it is dead too:

```js
export default defineConfigWithVueTs([
  includeIgnoreFile(gitignorePath),
  ...pluginVue.configs['flat/essential'],
  vueTsConfigs.recommendedTypeChecked
])
```

Then add the gate that would have caught this, as a step in `pr-build.yml`:

```yaml
      - run: npm run lint -- --no-fix
      - run: npm run type-check
```

Note `lint` is currently `eslint . --fix`; a CI gate must not autofix, so either
pass `--no-fix` or split the script into `lint` and `lint:fix`.

## Resolution
Deleted the trailing languageOptions block (parserOptions.project conflicted with projectService) and the empty override object. npm run lint now exits 0 and actually evaluates rules; wired @vue/eslint-config-prettier in, split lint/lint:fix so CI does not autofix, and added lint to pr-build.yml.
title: `npm run lint` fails with 14 errors and lints zero source files; no CI job runs it, so it went undetected

body:
## Problem

`tsconfig.json` lists `tsconfig.eslint.json` in `references`, so
`vue-tsc --build --force` builds it. Unlike the sibling configs it sets neither
`noEmit`, nor `outDir`, nor `composite`, so TypeScript emits JavaScript beside
every input file. `.gitignore` covers `dist` and `*.tsbuildinfo` but not these.

## Evidence

Isolating each referenced project shows exactly one is responsible:

```
$ rm -f vite.config.js src/main.js src/App.vue.js
$ npx vue-tsc --build --force tsconfig.app.json    ; ls …  ->  (nothing)
$ npx vue-tsc --build --force tsconfig.node.json   ; ls …  ->  (nothing)
$ npx vue-tsc --build --force tsconfig.eslint.json ; ls …  ->  src/App.vue.js src/main.js vite.config.js
```

Effective settings confirm the cause:

```
$ npx tsc --showConfig -p tsconfig.eslint.json   ->  noEmit: undefined  composite: undefined  outDir: undefined
$ npx tsc --showConfig -p tsconfig.app.json      ->  noEmit: true       composite: true
```

Running the documented command reproduces it from clean:

```
$ npm run type-check ; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
$ git status --porcelain -uall
?? src/App.vue.js
?? src/main.js
?? vite.config.js
```

`type-check` exits 0, so nothing signals the pollution.

## Impact

Every `npm run build` (which runs `type-check`) drops three untracked, unignored
generated files into the source tree. A `git add -A` commits compiled output
alongside the sources — and `vite.config.js` would then shadow `vite.config.ts`
for Vite's config resolution, silently freezing build configuration at whatever
was compiled. The files are also what ESLint chokes on in the lint finding.

## Fix

Make the lint-only project non-emitting, matching its siblings:

```json
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.app.json",
  "include": [...],
  "compilerOptions": {
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true,
    "strictNullChecks": true
  }
}
```

Better still: `tsconfig.eslint.json` exists only to widen the type-check surface
for ESLint, and `projectService` (see the ESLint finding) makes it unnecessary —
drop the file and its `references` entry entirely. Either way, delete the three
stray files (`rm -f vite.config.js src/main.js src/App.vue.js`) and add
`/vite.config.js`, `/src/**/*.js` to `.gitignore` as a backstop.

## Resolution
Deleted tsconfig.eslint.json and its references entry (projectService makes it unnecessary); added noEmit to the remaining projects and a /src/**/*.js .gitignore backstop. npm run build no longer drops .js into the source tree.
title: `npm run type-check` emits compiled .js next to the sources, and the files are neither ignored nor tracked

body:
## Problem

`pr-build.yml` installs with `npm ci || npm install` and calls
`actions/setup-node` without `node-version-file`. `build-and-deploy.yml` does the
opposite on both counts: plain `npm ci`, and `node-version-file: '.nvmrc'`.

## Evidence

```yaml
# pr-build.yml
      - uses: actions/setup-node@… # v6.5.0
        with:
          cache: 'npm'            # <- no node-version-file
      - run: npm ci || npm install
```
```yaml
# build-and-deploy.yml
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'   # 24.18.0
          cache: 'npm'
      - run: npm ci
```

`npm ci` is the command that *fails* when `package-lock.json` disagrees with
`package.json`. The `|| npm install` fallback catches that failure and rewrites
the lockfile in the runner, so the PR goes green. The deploy job on `main` has no
fallback and fails instead — after merge, on the branch that publishes.

The drift this masks is already present: the working tree carries 336 inserted /
337 deleted lines of uncommitted `package-lock.json` churn.

## Impact

Lockfile desync is invisible until it breaks production deployment, and the PR
build validates a dependency tree that neither the committed lockfile nor the
deploy job will use. Node version drift compounds it: PRs build on the runner's
default Node, deploys on 24.18.0, so a version-sensitive failure appears only
after merge.

## Fix

Make the PR job identical to the deploy job's install step:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6.5.0
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: 'npm'
      - run: npm ci
```

Dropping `|| npm install` is the whole point: a lockfile that cannot be installed
reproducibly should fail the PR, which is exactly what `npm ci` alone does.

## Resolution
pr-build.yml now uses node-version-file: '.nvmrc' and plain npm ci, matching build-and-deploy.yml exactly.
title: PR build masks lockfile drift with `npm ci || npm install` and does not pin Node, so it disagrees with the deploy job

body:
## Problem

The single verification step across all PR workflows is
`npm run build --if-present`. `--if-present` suppresses the error when the named
script does not exist, turning a missing `build` script into a successful run.
Combined with the broken `npm run lint` and the absence of any test script, this
is the repository's entire quality gate.

## Evidence

```yaml
      - run: npm run build --if-present
```

`npm run <script> --if-present` exits 0 when the script is absent — documented
npm behaviour, intended for optional lifecycle scripts in multi-package installs,
not for CI gates. A rename of `build` in `package.json` (e.g. to `build:prod`)
produces a green check with nothing built.

Nothing else gates: `pr-lint.yml` runs MegaLinter, not the project's own eslint
or tsc; `dependency-review.yml` scans manifests only; there is no test job.

## Impact

The gate can silently become a no-op through an ordinary `package.json` edit, and
there is no second check to notice. Type errors and lint failures already reach
`main` today because neither is run.

## Fix

Drop the flag and add the two checks that are supposed to be mandatory per
`AGENTS.md`:

```yaml
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint -- --no-fix
      - run: npm run type-check
      - run: npm run build
```

Plain `npm run build` fails loudly when the script is gone, which is the desired
behaviour for a required check.

## Resolution
Removed --if-present and added lint, type-check and test steps, so the PR gate fails loudly if any script is missing or failing.
title: `--if-present` makes the only PR gate silently pass if the build script disappears

body:
## Problem

The `CompressInPR` job sets `permissions: write-all`, granting every write scope
the `GITHUB_TOKEN` supports — including `actions`, `packages`, `deployments`,
`security-events`, and `id-token` — to a job whose only steps are `checkout` and
`calibreapp/image-actions`. Sibling workflows in the same repository scope
correctly: `compress-images.yml` requests just `contents: write`.

## Evidence

```yaml
  CompressInPR:
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions: write-all
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@…
      - uses: calibreapp/image-actions@…
        with:
          githubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Compare `compress-images.yml`, the same action, same purpose:

```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: write
```

The action's documented requirement is write access to repository contents (to
push the recompressed images) and pull requests (to comment). Nothing needs
`packages`, `deployments`, or `id-token`.

The fork guard limits this to same-repo PRs, which bounds who can trigger it but
not what the action can do once it runs.

## Impact

A compromised release of `calibreapp/image-actions` — or of anything in its
dependency tree — receives a token that can publish packages, create deployments,
write security events, and mint OIDC identity tokens for this repository. The pin
to SHA `9d037c0` mitigates tag-moving but not a compromise of that commit's
supply chain.

## Fix

Replace `write-all` with the two scopes the action actually uses:

```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
```

## Resolution
Replaced permissions: write-all with contents: write + pull-requests: write.
title: `permissions: write-all` grants a third-party image action the full token scope

body:
## Problem

`tsconfig.app.json` declares:

```json
  "vueCompilerOptions": {
    "plugins": ["@vue/typescript-plugin"]
  }
```

`@vue/typescript-plugin` is the tsserver/IDE plugin that powers Vue support in
editors. `vueCompilerOptions.plugins` expects `@vue/language-core` SFC-block
plugins. The declared plugin is loaded, rejected, and does nothing.

## Evidence

Every `npm run build` ends with:

```
[Vue] Plugin @vue/typescript-plugin is not compatible with the current Vue
language tools version. (version: undefined, supported versions: [2,2.1,2.2])
```

`version: undefined` is the plugin reporting no `@vue/language-core` API version
at all — it is not that kind of plugin. `package.json` pins
`"@vue/typescript-plugin": "^3.0.1"`, and the build still succeeds, so the
declaration is purely inert noise.

## Impact

A warning on every build and type-check run, training maintainers to ignore build
output — which is where the type-check pollution finding also surfaces. The
config also implies a compiler extension is active when none is.

## Fix

Delete the `vueCompilerOptions` block from `tsconfig.app.json`. If the intent was
editor Vue support, that is configured in the editor (`.vscode/extensions.json`
already recommends Volar) and needs no tsconfig entry — in which case
`@vue/typescript-plugin` can also come out of `devDependencies`.

## Resolution
Removed the vueCompilerOptions block from tsconfig.app.json and dropped @vue/typescript-plugin. The build no longer prints the incompatibility warning.
title: @vue/typescript-plugin is wired into vueCompilerOptions.plugins where it does not belong; every build prints an incompatibility warning

body:
## Problem

`"type-fix": "ts-standard --fix --project tsconfig.lint.json"` is a documented
command (`AGENTS.md:24`) backed by a package that has not been published in three
years and does not run against this repository.

## Evidence

```
$ npx ts-standard --project tsconfig.lint.json ; echo "exit=$?"
exit=1

$ npm view ts-standard time.modified version
time.modified = '2023-07-13T22:46:26.522Z'
version = '12.0.2'
```

Installed at `^12.0.2` — the same 2023 release; there is nothing newer to update
to. It bundles its own ESLint 8 tree beside the project's ESLint 10, including a
React plugin in a Vue application:

```
node_modules/ts-standard/node_modules/eslint-plugin-react
node_modules/ts-standard/node_modules/flat-cache
node_modules/ts-standard/node_modules/file-entry-cache
```

Those paths are among the `npm audit` advisory chains. `tsconfig.lint.json` exists
solely to serve this broken command.

`ts-standard` also enforces StandardJS formatting, which overlaps with the
project's Prettier config (`.prettierrc.json`) — two formatters, no precedence
declared.

## Impact

A documented workflow command fails for anyone who follows `AGENTS.md`. The
package contributes an abandoned ESLint 8 + React dependency subtree, and its
existence justifies a fifth tsconfig file that nothing else uses.

## Fix

Remove it. Prettier plus the (repaired) ESLint config already cover formatting and
style:

```
npm rm ts-standard
```

then delete the `type-fix` script from `package.json`, delete
`tsconfig.lint.json`, and drop the `yarn type-fix` line from `AGENTS.md`. Also fix
`AGENTS.md:22`, which mis-describes `type-lint` as "checks TypeScript using
ts-standard" — that script is `vue-tsc --noEmit`.

## Resolution
Removed ts-standard, the type-fix script and tsconfig.lint.json; dropped the stale type-lint entry from AGENTS.md. Prettier via ESLint now covers formatting.
title: `type-fix` is broken and ts-standard has been unmaintained since 2023, dragging eslint-plugin-react into a Vue project

body:
## Problem

Grepping every tracked file except `package.json` and `package-lock.json` for each
declared devDependency finds no reference to five of them.

## Evidence

```
@eslint/compat                ./eslint.config.mjs
@eslint/eslintrc              <<< NOT REFERENCED ANYWHERE >>>
@eslint/js                    <<< NOT REFERENCED ANYWHERE >>>
@tsconfig/node24              <<< NOT REFERENCED ANYWHERE >>>
vue-eslint-parser             <<< NOT REFERENCED ANYWHERE >>>
@vue/eslint-config-prettier   <<< NOT REFERENCED ANYWHERE >>>
eslint-plugin-vue             ./eslint.config.mjs
vite-plugin-vue-devtools      ./vite.config.ts
```

Per package:

- `@eslint/eslintrc` — the flat-config compat shim for `.eslintrc` files. The
  config is flat and `.gitignore` handling comes from `@eslint/compat`. Unused.
- `@eslint/js` — never imported; `eslint.config.mjs` builds on
  `defineConfigWithVueTs` instead.
- `@tsconfig/node24` — no tsconfig `extends` it. `tsconfig.node.json` hand-rolls
  `target`/`lib`/`module` instead, which is what the package exists to supply.
- `vue-eslint-parser` — arrives transitively via
  `@vue/eslint-config-typescript`; the direct declaration is redundant.
- `@vue/eslint-config-prettier` — **not imported by `eslint.config.mjs`**, so no
  Prettier rule is wired into ESLint at all. `AGENTS.md:11` states "Follow the
  style rules defined by Prettier and ESLint", describing an integration that
  does not exist.

(`@types/node` and `npm-run-all2` show no textual match but are genuinely used —
via `"types": ["node"]` in the tsconfigs and the `run-p` binary respectively.)

## Impact

Five packages installed and dependency-bot-maintained for nothing, on a project
with one 195-line component. `@vue/eslint-config-prettier` is worse than unused:
its presence in `package.json` is the only evidence for a documented convention
that is not enforced anywhere, so formatting drift goes uncaught.

## Fix

Drop the four dead ones:

```
npm rm @eslint/eslintrc @eslint/js @tsconfig/node24 vue-eslint-parser
```

Then decide `@vue/eslint-config-prettier` deliberately — either wire it in so the
documented convention is real:

```js
import prettier from '@vue/eslint-config-prettier'

export default defineConfigWithVueTs([
  includeIgnoreFile(gitignorePath),
  ...pluginVue.configs['flat/essential'],
  vueTsConfigs.recommendedTypeChecked,
  prettier
])
```

or remove it and drop the Prettier clause from `AGENTS.md:11`. Wiring it in is
the better call: `npm run format` already exists and would then be enforced
rather than advisory.

## Resolution
Removed @eslint/eslintrc, @eslint/js, @tsconfig/node24 and vue-eslint-parser. @vue/eslint-config-prettier is now imported in eslint.config.mjs, so the convention AGENTS.md documents is enforced. (@tsconfig/node24 was dropped rather than wired in: it sets module: nodenext, which conflicts with the Bundler resolution vite.config.ts needs.)
title: Five declared devDependencies are referenced nowhere, and one of them is the Prettier/ESLint integration AGENTS.md claims is active

body:
## Problem

The repository carries `tsconfig.json` (solution style, `files: []`),
`tsconfig.app.json`, `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.lint.json`, and
`tsconfig.eslint.json` — five configuration files for a project consisting of
`src/main.ts`, `src/App.vue`, `env.d.ts`, and `vite.config.ts`.

## Evidence

The `include` sets overlap and duplicate each other:

- `vite.config.ts` is claimed by **three** projects: `tsconfig.app.json`,
  `tsconfig.node.json` (`vite.config.*`), and `tsconfig.eslint.json`. Two of
  those are `composite`, so the same file belongs to two build graphs.
- `tsconfig.node.json` includes `vitest.config.*`, `cypress.config.*`,
  `nightwatch.conf.*`, and `playwright.config.*` — none of which exist.
- `tsconfig.eslint.json` and `tsconfig.lint.json` have near-identical `include`
  arrays and both restate `strict` / `strictNullChecks` already set by their base.
- `tsconfig.eslint.json` omits `noEmit`, which is what pollutes the source tree
  (filed separately).
- `tsconfig.lint.json` serves only `ts-standard`, which does not run (filed
  separately).

## Impact

Four of the five files are maintenance surface with no consumer, and the two
genuinely broken behaviours in the type-check pipeline both live in files that
exist only to support tooling that is either broken or redundant. Any change to
compiler options has to be reasoned about across five overlapping scopes.

## Fix

Collapse to the two-project layout the Vue/Vite toolchain expects — an app
project and a Node/tooling project — after the `ts-standard` and
`tsconfig.eslint.json` removals:

```
tsconfig.json         # references app + node only
tsconfig.app.json     # src/**/*, env.d.ts   (no vite.config.ts)
tsconfig.node.json    # vite.config.ts       (extends @tsconfig/node24, or drop that dep)
```

Give `vite.config.ts` to exactly one project — `tsconfig.node.json`, since it is
Node-side build tooling — and delete its entry from `tsconfig.app.json` along with
the four non-existent test-runner config globs.

## Resolution
Collapsed five tsconfigs to three: deleted tsconfig.eslint.json and tsconfig.lint.json, gave vite.config.ts to tsconfig.node.json only, and removed the four globs for absent test runners.
title: Five tsconfig files with overlapping include sets for one 195-line component; two are actively harmful

body:
## Problem

Job-level `permissions` **replaces** the workflow-level block rather than merging
with it. The workflow sets `permissions: read-all`, then the job sets only
`pull-requests: write`, so every other scope — including `contents` — becomes
`none` for that job.

## Evidence

```yaml
permissions: read-all          # workflow level

jobs:
  dependency-review:
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write     # replaces read-all entirely -> contents: none
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@…
      - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@…
```

`actions/dependency-review-action` documents its required permissions as
`contents: read` plus `pull-requests: write` (the latter only for
`comment-summary-in-pr`, which this workflow enables). The job currently grants
the second and not the first.

## Impact

The repository is public, so anonymous clone keeps `actions/checkout` working and
the job passes today. The moment the repository is made private — or the action
starts using the token for its dependency-graph API call — the job fails or
silently degrades, and the misconfiguration reads as intentional least-privilege.

## Fix

State both scopes explicitly:

```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
```

## Resolution
Restated contents: read alongside pull-requests: write in the job permissions block, with a comment noting that job-level permissions replace rather than merge.
title: dependency-review job omits the `contents: read` scope the action documents as required

body:
## Problem

The workflow triggers on `workflow_call` and on `pull_request` with
`types: [opened, reopened, synchronize]`. It has no `push` trigger for `main` and
does not include `closed` in the PR types, so nothing runs at the moment a PR
merges — which is when the draft's contents change.

## Evidence

```yaml
on:
  workflow_call
  # pull_request event is required only for autolabeler
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize]
```

Two problems in four lines:

1. The comment justifies the `pull_request` trigger as "required only for
   autolabeler", but `.github/release-drafter.yml` contains no `autolabeler:`
   block — only `categories`, `change-template`, `version-resolver`, and
   `template`. The stated reason for the trigger does not apply.
2. With no `push: branches: [main]` trigger and no `closed` type, the draft is
   only regenerated when the *next* PR is opened or pushed to. Merge PR #206 and
   the draft omits it until PR #207 appears.

`version-resolver` also resolves from labels (`major`/`minor`/`patch`,
`default: patch`) and ignores Conventional Commit markers, so the `!` in
`chore(deps)!:` subjects (commits a5defd6, 89996eb, 59f3b3a, 269bbac) has no
effect on the drafted version.

## Impact

The release draft always lags reality by one merged PR, so cutting a release
straight from the draft ships notes that omit the most recent change. The
misleading comment invites someone to "fix" the trigger by deleting it, which
would stop the drafter running at all.

## Fix

Add the trigger that actually corresponds to draft updates, and correct the
comment:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
```

Drop the `pull_request` trigger entirely unless an `autolabeler:` block is added
to `.github/release-drafter.yml` — in which case keep it and the comment becomes
true.

## Resolution
Replaced the pull_request trigger with push on main (plus workflow_dispatch), so the draft updates as each PR merges, and corrected the misleading autolabeler comment.
title: Release Drafter never runs after a merge, so the draft is permanently one PR stale; its autolabeler comment describes config that does not exist

body:
## Problem

`npm audit` reports 21 high-severity vulnerabilities. All of them are the same
advisory — a `brace-expansion` ReDoS/OOM (CWE-400, CWE-770) — reached through
ESLint's transitive tree. Commit 4794aff, "build(deps-dev): bump brace-expansion
from 1.1.15 to 1.1.16 (#208)", presents as the remediation but bumped a copy that
was never the vulnerable one.

## Evidence

```
$ npm audit --json | …
metadata: {"info":0,"low":0,"moderate":0,"high":21,"critical":0,"total":21}

brace-expansion @ <=5.0.7 (high)
  brace-expansion: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory
  process crash [high] CWE-400,CWE-770
  fixAvailable: {"name":"@eslint/eslintrc","version":"0.1.0","isSemVerMajor":true}
```

The installed copies show why the bump missed:

```
1.1.16  <- node_modules/brace-expansion/package.json                                    <- what #208 bumped
5.0.8   <- node_modules/eslint/node_modules/brace-expansion/package.json                <- vulnerable
5.0.8   <- node_modules/@eslint/config-array/node_modules/brace-expansion/package.json  <- vulnerable
5.0.8   <- node_modules/@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree/node_modules/brace-expansion/package.json
```

The advisory range is `<=5.0.7`, and the nested copies are 5.0.8 — i.e. already
past it — while the hoisted 1.x copy #208 moved is a different major line
entirely. The only `fixAvailable` npm can offer is a semver-major *downgrade* of
`@eslint/eslintrc` to 0.1.0, which is not a fix.

Everything in the chain is `devDependencies`. The production bundle is Vue only:
`dist/assets/index-jcAEBoAY.js` is 67 kB and contains no ESLint code.

## Impact

No runtime exposure — nothing here ships to users. The real cost is a permanently
red `npm audit` that cannot be cleared, which trains maintainers to ignore audit
output, and a merged commit whose message asserts a fix that did not occur.

## Fix

Record it as accepted rather than chase it. Two concrete steps:

1. Remove `ts-standard` and the four unused `@eslint/*` / parser packages (filed
   separately) — that deletes several of the 21 advisory paths outright. Re-run
   `npm audit` afterwards to see the real remainder.
2. For what remains, note the accepted risk (dev-only, no upstream fix) with
   `.github/renovate.json` `vulnerabilityAlerts` config or an `npm audit
   --omit=dev` gate, so audit output stays actionable.

Do not run `npm audit fix`: its only proposal is the `@eslint/eslintrc`
downgrade.

## Resolution
Resolved as a side effect of removing ts-standard and the unused @eslint/* packages: npm audit now reports 'found 0 vulnerabilities', down from 21 high.
title: All 21 high-severity npm advisories are one dev-only CVE, and the commit that claimed to fix it did not

body:
## Problem

`package-lock.json` is modified in the working tree — 336 insertions, 337
deletions — while `package.json` is untouched. The diff is pure transitive
version movement, which means someone ran `npm install` (not `npm ci`) and the
resulting resolution drift was never committed or reverted.

## Evidence

```
$ git diff --stat
 package-lock.json | 673 +++++++++++++-------------------
 1 file changed, 336 insertions(+), 337 deletions(-)

$ git diff -U0 package-lock.json | …   # packages entering/leaving the tree
added-only:   (none)
removed-only: (none)
```

No package is added or removed — only versions move:

```
-      "version": "4.9.1",    +      "version": "4.10.1",   # @eslint-community/eslint-utils
-      "version": "0.6.0",    +      "version": "0.7.0",    # @eslint/config-helpers
-      "version": "3.3.5",    +      "version": "3.3.6",    # @eslint/eslintrc
-      "version": "0.138.0",  +      "version": "…",        # @oxc-project/types
```

This is precisely the drift that `npm ci || npm install` in `pr-build.yml`
(filed separately) would hide: the fallback regenerates the lockfile in CI, so a
PR carrying this state builds green.

## Impact

An unreviewed dependency-resolution change is sitting in the working tree on
branch `feat/upgrades`. Committed accidentally, it lands transitive upgrades that
Renovate never proposed and no PR reviewed; discarded, whatever prompted the
`npm install` is lost. Either way the tree does not match any reviewed state.

## Fix

Decide it explicitly. To keep the current, tested resolution:

```
git add package-lock.json
git commit -m "chore(deps): refresh transitive lockfile resolutions"
```

To return to the reviewed state:

```
git checkout -- package-lock.json && npm ci
```

Prefer `npm ci` over `npm install` for routine local installs so the lockfile
stops drifting as a side effect.

## Resolution
Lockfile committed as part of this change set; the transitive churn is now subsumed by the deliberate add of vitest and removal of six packages. pr-build.yml no longer has the npm install fallback that would have hidden future drift.
title: Uncommitted lockfile churn in the working tree with no package.json change

## Problem

There is no test script, no test framework, and no test file anywhere in the
repository. `AGENTS.md:28` states "No automated tests are defined." The app's
whole function is to emit a shell script; nothing verifies that the emitted script
is correct, parses, or runs.

## Evidence

`package.json` `scripts` contains `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `build-only`,
`type-check`, `lint`, `type-lint`, `type-fix`, `format` — no `test`.

Meanwhile the configuration pretends a test setup exists:

- `tsconfig.node.json` includes `vitest.config.*`, `cypress.config.*`,
  `nightwatch.conf.*`, `playwright.config.*` — none present.
- `tsconfig.app.json` excludes `src/**/__tests__/*` — no such directory.
- `.gitignore` ignores `/cypress/videos/`, `/cypress/screenshots/`, `coverage`.
- `.github/linters/.jscpd.json` ignores `**/__snapshots__/**`.

Three separate Critical/High defects in this audit are mechanically detectable and
would each have been caught on the first run of a minimal suite:

| Defect | Detector that would have caught it |
| --- | --- |
| `$NAME` never assigned | `shellcheck -s sh` → SC2154 |
| `&>` bashism | `shellcheck -s sh` → SC2039/SC3000-range, or `dash -n` |
| non-POSIX `local` / `echo -n` | `shellcheck -s sh` → SC3043, SC3037 |
| unescaped input | one golden-file assertion on a name containing `;` |

`shellcheck` reports 7 warnings and 15 notes on the default output today.

## Impact

The only artifact the app produces has never been mechanically validated, and
three defects that make it non-functional shipped to a deployed GitHub Pages site.
Every fix in this audit is also unprotected against regression — including the
shell-quoting fix, which is exactly the kind of change that silently rots.

## Fix

The generator is a pure function of four strings, so the test is cheap. Add Vitest
and two specs:

```
npm i -D vitest
```

```json
  "scripts": {
    "test": "vitest run"
  }
```

1. **Golden output** — extract the substitution into a `fill()` helper (see the
   `computed` finding), then assert the generated script for known inputs against
   a committed snapshot, plus explicit cases for a name containing `;`, a space,
   and a description containing a newline.
2. **Shell validation** — in the same spec, write the generated script to a temp
   file and assert `shellcheck -s sh` and `dash -n` both exit 0. That turns every
   POSIX-compliance finding here into a permanent gate.

Then wire `npm test` into `pr-build.yml` alongside lint and type-check.

## Resolution
Added vitest plus 31 tests across two specs. src/__tests__/service-template.spec.ts covers quoting, sanitising, validation, golden output and regression guards for the $NAME/&>/POSIX defects, and runs shellcheck -s sh -S warning and dash -n over four input variants. src/__tests__/App.spec.ts covers the a11y names and validation gating. npm test is now a step in pr-build.yml.
title: No tests at all, while the product's entire output is a shell script that is currently broken three independent ways

## Problem

The file agents and contributors are told to follow contains three statements that
contradict the repository.

## Evidence

1. **Node version** — `AGENTS.md:12`: "Node.js version is controlled via `.nvmrc`
   (22.17.0)". `.nvmrc` contains `24.18.0`. The stated version is four majors
   behind, and `.nvmrc` has been bumped twice recently (0e38221, 19fdb54) without
   the doc following.

2. **`type-lint`** — `AGENTS.md:22`: "`yarn type-lint`   # checks TypeScript using
   ts-standard". `package.json:13` defines it as
   `vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.lint.json`. `ts-standard` is used by `type-fix`
   (line 14), a different script — which does not run (exits 1, filed
   separately).

3. **Mandated lint** — `AGENTS.md:9`: "Run linting and type checks before
   committing any code changes." `npm run lint` fails with 14 parse errors and
   lints zero source files (filed separately), so the instruction cannot be
   satisfied by anyone who follows it.

`AGENTS.md:11` additionally claims Prettier style rules are followed via ESLint,
but `@vue/eslint-config-prettier` is never imported into `eslint.config.mjs`.

## Impact

This is the file that configures agent behaviour on this repository. An agent
following it installs the wrong Node, believes a passing `type-lint` covered
StandardJS style when it only ran `tsc`, and hits an unpassable lint gate before
every commit — the most likely resolution being to skip the check, which is how
the broken ESLint config survived.

## Fix

Correct all three, and make the version claim non-duplicating:

```md
- Node.js version is controlled via `.nvmrc`.
...
yarn lint        # runs ESLint with autofix
yarn type-check  # type-checks the app with vue-tsc
yarn format      # formats using Prettier
```

Drop the `type-lint`/`type-fix` lines together with `ts-standard` itself, and
restate line 9 once `npm run lint` passes. Omitting the literal version number
stops the doc drifting from `.nvmrc` again.

## Resolution
Corrected all three: dropped the hardcoded Node version (now points at .nvmrc), removed the wrong type-lint/ts-standard description, and restated the pre-commit checks now that lint passes. Added a section on the shell-quoting rules for the generated script.
title: AGENTS.md is wrong on the Node version, on what type-lint does, and mandates a lint step that cannot pass

body:
## Problem

The documented developer workflow is Yarn. The actual dependency management is
npm. Nothing reconciles them, and the one file that would make Yarn reproducible
is explicitly ignored.

## Evidence

Documented (`README.md:18-30`, `AGENTS.md:8,16-26`):

```bash
yarn install
yarn dev
yarn lint
yarn build
```

Actual state:

- `package-lock.json` is committed (8281 lines, `lockfileVersion: 3`).
- `.gitignore:34-35` ignores `yarn.lock` and `.yarn/`.
- `.yarnrc.yml` exists (`nodeLinker: node-modules`) — so Yarn is half-configured.
- Every workflow installs with npm: `build-and-deploy.yml` runs `npm ci` with
  `cache: 'npm'`; `pr-build.yml` runs `npm ci || npm install`.
- Dependabot/Renovate commits touch `package-lock.json` only (4794aff, a95ecfb,
  5ceac6d, 50422bb).

So a developer following the README runs `yarn install`, which ignores
`package-lock.json`, resolves fresh versions, and writes a `yarn.lock` that git
discards.

## Impact

Documented setup and CI install different dependency trees, and the local tree is
unpinned across machines. "Works locally, fails in CI" (and the reverse) has no
diagnosable cause, because the lockfile that would explain it is ignored. This is
the same class of problem as the uncommitted lockfile churn already in the tree.

## Fix

Pick npm — CI, both lockfile-bearing workflows, and every bot commit already use
it. Rewrite the README and AGENTS.md commands:

```bash
npm ci        # once
npm run dev
npm run lint
npm run build
```

Then delete `.yarnrc.yml` and drop the `yarn.lock` / `.yarn/` entries from
`.gitignore`, since nothing should produce them.

If Yarn is genuinely wanted instead, the inverse is required: commit `yarn.lock`,
delete `package-lock.json`, and switch every workflow to
`yarn install --immutable` with `cache: 'yarn'`. That is strictly more work for
no gain here.

## Resolution
Standardised on npm across README.md and AGENTS.md, deleted .yarnrc.yml, and removed the yarn.lock/.yarn/.pnp entries from .gitignore. Also corrected the README usage steps to reference the app's own shell-commands panel and the logrotate output.
title: README and AGENTS.md prescribe Yarn, but the repo commits package-lock.json, gitignores yarn.lock, and every CI job uses npm

body:
## Problem

`public/site.webmanifest` declares both name fields as empty strings and omits
`start_url` and `scope`, while `index.html:12` links it as the page manifest.

## Evidence

```json
{
  "name": "",
  "short_name": "",
  "icons": [ … ],
  "theme_color": "#ffffff",
  "background_color": "#ffffff",
  "display": "standalone"
}
```

`index.html:14` has the real title (`sysvinit service generator`) and `:6` a
description, so the information exists — it just was never copied into the
manifest. The app deploys under a sub-path
(`vite.config.ts:15`, `base: '/sysvinit-service-generator/'`), which is exactly
the case where a missing `start_url`/`scope` matters, since both default relative
to the manifest's own location rather than to a declared app root.

## Impact

Installing the site as a PWA produces a home-screen entry with a blank label. With
`display: standalone` and no `scope`, navigation boundaries are implicit, so
behaviour on the GitHub Pages sub-path depends on browser defaults.

## Fix

Fill in the fields that already exist elsewhere in the repo:

```json
{
  "name": "sysvinit service generator",
  "short_name": "sysvinit gen",
  "start_url": "/sysvinit-service-generator/",
  "scope": "/sysvinit-service-generator/",
  "display": "standalone",
  "theme_color": "#ffffff",
  "background_color": "#ffffff",
  "icons": [ … ]
}
```

## Resolution
Filled in name, short_name, start_url and scope in public/site.webmanifest, using the sub-path the Vite base option deploys to.
title: Web app manifest has empty name and short_name, and no start_url or scope

body:
## Problem

`README.md:39` credits `yunginnanet/sysvinit-service-generator` under
"Acknowledgments", and the init-script template in `src/App.vue` is
recognisably derived from it. `LICENSE` carries only
`Copyright (c) 2024 Ismo Vuorinen`. MIT requires that the copyright notice and
permission notice be retained in copies and substantial portions of the work.

## Evidence

Upstream's license is confirmed MIT and the project is active:

```
$ gh api repos/yunginnanet/sysvinit-service-generator --jq '{license:.license.spdx_id, archived:.archived}'
{"archived":false,"license":"MIT","name":"yunginnanet/sysvinit-service-generator"}
```

MIT-to-MIT is fully compatible, so there is no licensing conflict — only a missing
attribution. The dependency tree is clean on this front: 377 MIT, 24 ISC, 19
Apache-2.0, 8 BSD-2-Clause, 3 BSD-3-Clause, 2 MPL-2.0, 1 Python-2.0, 1 CC-BY-4.0,
and no GPL/AGPL/LGPL/SSPL/BUSL anywhere. Nine packages declare no license field.
The bundled Inter-derived favicon is correctly attributed under OFL-1.1 in
`public/favicon.txt`.

The `LICENSE` copyright year is also 2024, two years stale.

## Impact

An MIT term is unmet — minor in practice, trivial to correct, and awkward for a
project that publishes a `LICENSE` file and an acknowledgments section.

## Fix

Add the upstream notice to `LICENSE` above the existing one:

```
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2024-2026 Ismo Vuorinen
Portions derived from https://github.com/yunginnanet/sysvinit-service-generator
Copyright (c) yunginnanet, MIT License
```

Optionally note which part is derived (the init-script template in
`src/App.vue`), and check the nine undeclared-license packages if the project ever
needs a clean SBOM.

## Resolution
Added the upstream MIT copyright notice and the derivation note to LICENSE, and updated the copyright year range.
title: Derived from an MIT-licensed upstream project without carrying its copyright notice
